name: Spinal Tuberculosis / Pott Disease
definition: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving vertebral bodies, discs and/or paraspinal tissues, potentially causing collapse, deformity, abscess and spinal cord or nerve-root compression.

typical: Constitutional symptoms may be mild or absent
Paraspinal or psoas abscess may occur

investigations.principle: Microbiological confirmation and drug-susceptibility testing are important where feasible.
investigations.MRI: MRI defines vertebral/disc, epidural and paraspinal involvement and neural compression.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs/CT help define collapse, deformity and bony destruction.

green: Prompt tuberculosis treatment under national/local protocol
Orthopedic/spine review for instability, deformity or deficit
amber: Surgery is indicated selectively for severe/progressive neurological compression, instability, deformity or failure of medical management.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi/Majja-gata infection-related frameworks may be documented only in parallel; anti-tubercular therapy must not be delayed.

patientEducation.summary: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving vertebral bodies, discs and/or paraspinal tissues, potentially causing collapse, deformity, abscess and spinal cord or nerve-root compression.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, breathing/swallowing difficulty, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
